query: how to build a customer requests desk from your inbox
title: Build a customer requests desk from your inbox | 50agents
description: Turn your inbox into a requests desk: one record per request with status, priority and an answer-by date, a board by status, and replies drafted.
h1: How to build a customer requests desk from your inbox
answer: Give every customer email that needs an answer a record with a status, a priority and an answer-by date.
Then work from a board of those records instead of the inbox.

root.q: How many people answer customer email?

options.label: Just me, a few a day

then.why: Free and nothing new to learn. You get no answer-by dates and no view of what is late, so check the label daily.

then.q: Do you want replies drafted for you?

then.why: Google Groups Collaborative Inbox, Front or Hiver let you assign each email to one person and filter what is unresolved.
It turns each email into a record, sorts it by kind and priority, and drafts a reply that waits for your yes.

then.answer: A help desk such as Zendesk or Freshdesk
then.why: Tickets, service-level targets, macros and reports across email, chat and phone. Heavy for a small team.

method.h2: How to build a customer requests desk, step by step

steps.title: Pick one address for requests
steps.body: support@ or help@. Requests sent to personal inboxes get lost when someone is away.

steps.title: Decide what becomes a request
steps.body: A question, a problem, a change, a complaint. Not newsletters, invoices or sales pitches.

steps.title: Create a record per request
steps.body: By hand from a label, or automatically from new email. Keep the thread link on the record.

steps.title: Sort each one as it arrives
steps.body: Set kind, priority and answer-by date. Rules first, then judgement for the unclear ones.

note.text: Write the rule for Urgent in one sentence: something is broken, money is at stake, or the customer is upset. Otherwise everything drifts to urgent.

steps.title: Work from the board
steps.body: Waiting on us, oldest first, urgent at the top. The inbox becomes where replies go out, not where work is tracked.

steps.title: Close the loop
steps.body: Waiting on them for three days with no reply: send a short check-in, then mark it Solved.

captain.line: Captain builds the desk with an AI agent that sorts each new request, drafts a reply from what your business knows, and waits for your yes.

wrong.title: Two people answer the same email
wrong.body: Nobody could see who had it. Assign each request to one person, or have one person own the desk.

wrong.title: A thread splits
wrong.body: The customer replies with a new subject and it becomes a new request. Match on the customer's email and merge.

wrong.title: Forwarded requests lose the customer
wrong.body: A colleague forwards an email and the record shows the colleague as the customer. Read the original sender from the forwarded text.

wrong.title: Drafts that promise too much
wrong.body: An AI-drafted reply offers a refund you would not give. Keep your policies in its memory, and review every draft before it goes.

faqs.a: A shared inbox for a small team with modest volume; a help desk once you have many support staff, several channels or service-level targets to report on.

faqs.q: How do I stop two people replying to the same email?
faqs.a: Assign each conversation to one person. Google Groups' Collaborative Inbox lets members take a conversation; a desk app shows each request's owner and status.

faqs.q: How do I track open customer requests?
faqs.a: Give each one a record with a status and an answer-by date, and work from a view of everything Waiting on us, oldest first.
